Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination  
Member: Reese Kimura  
Member ID: W325265581  
Reference number: POC-BF385BB269-48000  
Requested service: Bunion surgery for hallux valgus  
CPT: 28296  
Date of denial notice: August 14, 2026

Dear CountyCare Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal CountyCare’s denial of prior authorization for CPT 28296, correction of hallux valgus with bunionectomy and distal metatarsal osteotomy. The denial states that the submitted imaging does not support medical necessity. The clinical record demonstrates a painful, progressive deformity with objective radiographic findings, persistent symptoms despite extensive conservative treatment, and significant functional impairment.

The submitted imaging supports the requested procedure:

- Weight-bearing foot radiographs dated July 11, 2026 show a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees.
- The same radiographs show an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees.
- The patient has a documented prominence with ulceration risk.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, and range of motion was limited by pain.

The patient has also had symptoms for 12 months, with progressive foot pain that has not been relieved by rest. The condition prevents the patient from tolerating closed shoes and interferes with ordinary function.

Conservative treatment has been attempted and was unsuccessful:

- Activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic were used for 10 weeks, from May 6, 2026 through July 15, 2026.
- The patient completed 16 physical therapy visits, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- NSAIDs were used for four months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on June 2, 2026 provided only three weeks of partial relief.

The patient’s clinical status also supports proceeding with surgery. There is no active infection, untreated substance use, or smoking history. BMI is 29. The patient has persistent pain, restricted painful motion, inability to wear closed shoes, and risk of ulceration over the deformity.

The denial does not identify the specific imaging measurement, clinical criterion, or missing documentation that CountyCare believes is required. I request that CountyCare reconsider the denial based on the enclosed radiographs and clinical records. If CountyCare continues to rely on medical-necessity criteria, please provide the exact policy and clinical review criteria applied to this request, including the applicable policy title, policy number, version or effective date, and the specific reason the July 11, 2026 radiographs were considered insufficient.

No CountyCare policy text is quoted in this appeal because I was unable to identify a publicly available CountyCare policy containing the applicable criteria for CPT 28296. This appeal instead addresses the stated denial reason using the clinical evidence submitted with the prior authorization request.

Please overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 28296. If additional information is needed, please contact the treating surgeon, Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery, or notify me in writing of the specific information required.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the appeal determination in writing.

Sincerely,

Reese Kimura  
Member ID: W325265581  
[Telephone number]  
[Mailing address]

Enclosures:

- July 11, 2026 weight-bearing foot radiographs and report
- Physical therapy discharge note documenting 16 visits from May 6, 2026 through July 15, 2026
- Documentation of NSAID treatment
- June 2, 2026 corticosteroid injection record
- Orthopedic examination and surgical recommendation
- Copy of the adverse benefit determination notice
